---
title: X5 Prepare a reusable output
subtitle: Optional extension · self-paced · about 35 minutes
description: Add the synthetic dataset and its data dictionary, correct the citation and licence metadata, record the rights decision, and publish a demo release.
---

::: {.callout-tip title="Optional extension"}
The [core workflow](../syllabus.qmd#core) ends with X4. This exercise is an optional, self-paced extension. Start it in the block "Consolidate and extend", or later, when your thesis needs it. It uses the Issues E08-S1, E08-T2, and E08-T3 from [X2](x2.qmd) and the pull request routine from [X4](x4.qmd). It does not need X6. No assessment requires it.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
- **Time:** about 35 minutes
- **You produce:** the CSV in `data/clean/`, a data dictionary that closes the story E08-S1, optionally a corrected `CITATION.cff`, a rights and access decision (E08-T2), and the release `v0.1.0-demo` (E08-T3).
- **New terms:** [release](../cheat-sheet.qmd#release), [tag](../cheat-sheet.qmd#tag), [visibility](../cheat-sheet.qmd#visibility). All terms are in the [cheat sheet](../cheat-sheet.qmd).
:::

## Why this step

Data become reusable only with documentation. A future reuser needs to know what each column means, how missing values appear, where the data come from, which version they hold, and under which licence they may reuse them. The user story E08-S1 states exactly this need.

Publication is a decision, not a side effect. Before you publish, decide for each output who may see it and under which terms, and note the rights of others. In the scenario, a fictional archive restricts its scans. The scans therefore stay outside the repository.

A **release** marks a state of the repository with a version and notes. It is useful for citation within a project, but it is **not long-term preservation**. GitHub can delete or change a repository. A **deposit** in a repository such as Zenodo, with a DOI, is a separate step that this workshop does not perform. See [Publication](../../documentation/publication.qmd).

Five jobs are easy to confuse. Each one needs its own place, and one tool does not do the job of another.

| Job | Question | Where | Not the same as |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Coordination | Who does what, by when? | Issues and the Project | Storage |
| Storage | Where do the working data live? | Here: the synthetic data in the repository. Real data: where your institution allows | Publication |
| Publication | What may others see and reuse? | A public repository, a release, or GitHub Pages, after the rights decision | Preservation |
| Backup | Can I restore my work after a loss? | A second copy outside GitHub | An exported view or a release |
| Preservation | Will it still exist, and be citable, in ten years? | A deposit with a DOI, for example on Zenodo | A release |

## Before you start

- Browser route: download the [synthetic CSV](../../data/synthetic-periodicals.csv) to your computer.
- Browser route: note the Issue numbers of E08-S1, E08-T2, and E08-T3.
- Command-line route: open a terminal in the folder `projm-thesis`. Run `git pull` to get the latest state. Define the helper `issue` as in [X3](x3.qmd#before-you-start), if this is a new terminal:

  ```bash
  issue() { gh issue list --state all --limit 100 --json number,title \
    --jq ".[] | select(.title | startswith(\"$1 \")) | .number"; }
  ```

## Steps

### Add the dataset and the data dictionary

::: {.panel-tabset group="route"}

#### Browser

1. In your repository, open the folder `data/clean`.
2. Click **Add file → Upload files**. Drop `synthetic-periodicals.csv`.
3. Select **Create a new branch for this commit and start a pull request**. Click **Propose changes**.
4. On the new branch, open `documentation/data-dictionary.template.qmd` and click the pencil icon.
5. In the file name field, rename the file to `data-dictionary.qmd`.
6. Replace the text with the [example data dictionary](#data-dictionary-text) below.
7. Commit to the same branch.
8. Open a pull request with the description `Closes #<number of E08-S1>`. Review it and merge it as in [X4](x4.qmd).

#### Command line

1. Create a branch and switch to it:

   ```bash
   git switch -c docs/e08-s1-data-dictionary
   ```

2. Download the CSV from the course repository into the folder `data/clean`:

   ```bash
   gh api repos/maehr/github-as-a-project-management-tool/contents/data/synthetic-periodicals.csv \
     -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw" > data/clean/synthetic-periodicals.csv
   ```

3. Rename the template of the data dictionary:

   ```bash
   git mv documentation/data-dictionary.template.qmd documentation/data-dictionary.qmd
   ```

4. Open `documentation/data-dictionary.qmd` in a text editor.
5. Replace the text with the [example data dictionary](#data-dictionary-text) below.
6. Save the file.
7. Save both files as a commit and send the branch to GitHub. git can warn that LF will be replaced by CRLF. The template sets this line ending for CSV files, so you can ignore the warning.

   ```bash
   git add data/clean/synthetic-periodicals.csv documentation/data-dictionary.qmd
   git commit -m "docs: document the dataset for a future reuser"
   git push -u origin docs/e08-s1-data-dictionary
   ```

8. Open the pull request, review it, and merge it as in [X4](x4.qmd). The description closes E08-S1:

   ```bash
   gh pr create --title "docs: document the dataset for a future reuser" --body "Closes #$(issue E08-S1)"
   gh pr review --comment --body "Checked the columns, the missing values, and the licence."
   gh pr merge --merge --delete-branch
   ```

:::

### Optional: correct the citation file

Skip this step if you are short of time. Do it before you publish a real release.


The file `CITATION.cff` in your repository still describes the **template**, with its authors and its DOI. Anyone who clicks **Cite this repository** gets the wrong reference.

::: {.panel-tabset group="route"}

#### Browser

1. Open `CITATION.cff` and click the pencil icon.
2. Replace the text with the [citation text](#citation-text) below.
3. Commit with the message `docs: describe this repository in CITATION.cff`.
4. Check that the licence files `LICENSE-CCBY.md` and `LICENSE-AGPL.md` exist. They match the licence line in the README.

#### Command line

1. Open `CITATION.cff` in a text editor.
2. Replace the text with the [citation text](#citation-text) below.
3. Save the file.
4. Save the change as a commit and send it to GitHub:

   ```bash
   git add CITATION.cff
   git commit -m "docs: describe this repository in CITATION.cff"
   git push
   ```

5. Check that the licence files exist. The list shows `LICENSE-AGPL.md` and `LICENSE-CCBY.md`. They match the licence line in the README.

   ```bash
   ls LICENSE-*
   ```

:::

### Record the rights and access decision

::: {.panel-tabset group="route"}

#### Browser

1. Open the folder `project-management`.
2. If the folder holds `decisions.md`, for example from X6, open the file and click the pencil icon. Paste the [decision text](#decision-text) below at the end.
3. If the folder holds no `decisions.md`, click **Add file → Create new file** and name it `decisions.md`. Type `# Decisions` on the first line. Paste the [decision text](#decision-text) below.
4. Commit with the message `docs: record the rights and access decision` and the extended description `Closes #<number of E08-T2>`.

#### Command line

1. Create the file `project-management/decisions.md` with the heading `# Decisions` if it is missing. If the file exists, for example from X6, the command does nothing.

   ```bash
   test -f project-management/decisions.md || echo "# Decisions" > project-management/decisions.md
   ```

2. Open `project-management/decisions.md` in a text editor. Paste the [decision text](#decision-text) below at the end.
3. Save the file.
4. Save the file as a commit and send it to GitHub. The second `-m` adds the extended description. Its keyword closes E08-T2 when the commit reaches `main`.

   ```bash
   git add project-management/decisions.md
   git commit -m "docs: record the rights and access decision" -m "Closes #$(issue E08-T2)"
   git push
   ```

:::

### Publish the demo release

::: {.callout-warning title="A release publishes more than its notes"}
GitHub adds two source archives (`.zip` and `.tar.gz`) to every release. They contain every tracked file of the repository at the tag, not only the files that the release notes name. Check the file list of the repository before you publish. In a private repository, the release stays private.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset group="route"}

#### Browser

1. On the repository home page, click **Create a new release** (right column, under **Releases**).
2. Click **Choose a tag**, type `v0.1.0-demo`, and select **Create new tag**.
3. Type the title `v0.1.0-demo: documented synthetic dataset (demo)`.
4. Paste the [release notes](#release-notes) below.
5. Click **Publish release**.
6. Open E08-T3, write a comment with the link to the release, and click **Close issue**.

{{< screenshot x5-release >}}

#### Command line

1. Save the [release notes](#release-notes) below as `release-notes.md` in the folder that contains `projm-thesis`.
2. Create the release. gh creates the tag `v0.1.0-demo` on `main` and prints the address of the release.

   ```bash
   gh release create v0.1.0-demo --title "v0.1.0-demo: documented synthetic dataset (demo)" \
     --notes-file ../release-notes.md
   ```

3. Close E08-T3 with a link to the release. `gh release view` finds the address of the release.

   ```bash
   gh issue close $(issue E08-T3) --comment "Released: $(gh release view v0.1.0-demo --json url --jq .url)"
   ```

:::

## Texts to copy

### Data dictionary text {#data-dictionary-text}

```markdown
---
title: Data Dictionary
description: Structure, variables, and definitions of the synthetic periodical metadata.
---

This document describes `data/clean/synthetic-periodicals.csv`.

**Every record is synthetic.** The records describe periodicals that never existed.

## Overview

- **Title**: Synthetic periodical metadata, Switzerland, 1830–1960
- **Authors**: Fictional MA student (workshop example)
- **Version**: 1.0.0 (2026-10-16)
- **License**: CC BY 4.0

## Methodology

A script generated the 30 records with a fixed seed for the workshop. No record comes from a real archive.

## Missing values

Missing values are empty cells: `last_year` (5 records), `publisher` (3 records), `frequency` (2 records).

## Definitions

| Variable Name          | Description                                  | Data Type | Allowed Values                                                           |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `record_id`            | Unique identifier of the record              | String    | `SYN-P001` to `SYN-P030`                                                 |
| `title`                | Title of the fictional periodical            | String    | Free text                                                                |
| `language`             | Main language (ISO 639-1)                    | String    | `de`, `fr`, `it`                                                         |
| `place_of_publication` | Town of publication                          | String    | Free text                                                                |
| `first_year`           | First year of publication                    | Integer   | 1830 to 1905                                                             |
| `last_year`            | Last year of publication                     | Integer   | Empty if not known                                                       |
| `frequency`            | Frequency of publication                     | String    | `daily`, `weekly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `irregular`; empty if unknown |
| `subject`              | Main subject                                 | String    | `politics`, `culture`, `religion`, `economy`, `science`, `entertainment` |
| `publisher`            | Fictional publisher or printer               | String    | Free text; empty if not known                                            |
| `scan_reuse_status`    | Reuse terms of the fictional archive's scans | String    | `open`, `attribution-required`, `unknown`, `restricted`                  |
| `digitised`            | Digitisation status                          | String    | `yes`, `no`, `partial`                                                   |
| `is_synthetic`         | Marks the record as synthetic                | Boolean   | `true`                                                                   |
```

### Citation text {#citation-text}

```yaml
cff-version: 1.2.0
title: "Fictional master's thesis: Swiss periodicals, 1830–1960 (workshop example)"
message: >-
  This is a teaching example with synthetic data. Cite the workshop, not
  this repository, if you refer to it.
type: dataset
authors:
  - given-names: Fictional
    family-names: Student
license: CC-BY-4.0
abstract: >-
  Workshop example: 30 synthetic periodical records and the plan of a fictional
  DH master's thesis, managed with GitHub Issues and a GitHub Project.
```

### Decision text {#decision-text}

```markdown
## D-T01 Rights and access for data and text

- **Date:** 2026-10-16 (workshop; fictional)
- **Context:** The thesis produces a CSV, a data dictionary, and the thesis text. The fictional archive states reuse terms for its scans.
- **Decision:**

  | Output                                 | Access                           | Licence             |
  | -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------- |
  | `data/clean/synthetic-periodicals.csv` | Public                           | CC BY 4.0           |
  | `documentation/data-dictionary.qmd`    | Public                           | CC BY 4.0           |
  | Scans of the fictional archive         | Not in the repository            | Archive terms       |
  | Thesis text                            | Private until the grade is final | All rights reserved |

- **Library access to the thesis:** The author and the supervisor decide together (RSL Phil.-hist. 21 Art. 32 Abs. 1).
```

### Release notes {#release-notes}

```markdown
**Demo release for the workshop. The data are synthetic.**

## Contents

- `data/clean/synthetic-periodicals.csv`: 30 synthetic records (CC BY 4.0)
- `documentation/data-dictionary.qmd`: columns, types, missing values, version, licence

## Limits

- A GitHub release is not long-term preservation. A repository deposit with a DOI is a separate step.
- This release contains only material that decision D-T01 allows.
```

## Expected state

- [ ] `data/clean/synthetic-periodicals.csv` and `documentation/data-dictionary.qmd` are on `main`; E08-S1 is closed.
- [ ] **Cite this repository** shows the fictional thesis, not the template.
- [ ] `project-management/decisions.md` holds D-T01; E08-T2 is closed.
- [ ] The release `v0.1.0-demo` exists; E08-T3 is closed with a link to it.
- [ ] The Project shows the three Issues as **Done**.

## If something goes wrong

| Problem | Cause | Recovery |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The CSV download fails on the command line. | No connection, or a typing error in the path. | Open the [CSV](../../data/synthetic-periodicals.csv) in the browser and save it as `data/clean/synthetic-periodicals.csv`. |
| The CSV upload fails. | The browser blocked the download. | Open the [CSV](../../data/synthetic-periodicals.csv), copy all lines, and create the file with **Add file → Create new file**. |
| The file name field does not rename. | The cursor was in the editor. | Click the file name field above the editor, then edit the name. |
| The commit did not close E08-T2. | The keyword was in the title, or the commit is on another branch. | Close the Issue by hand with a link to the commit. |
| **Create a new release** is missing. | The right column is collapsed. | Open `https://github.com/<you>/projm-thesis/releases/new`. |
| You have no time for the release. | — | Use the **recovery package**: download the repository ZIP (**Code → Download ZIP**) and name it `projm-thesis-v0.1.0-demo-recovery.zip`. Label it as a recovery package, not as a release. |
| A command fails. | Usually the installation, the sign-in, or the folder. | See [Command-line problems](../setup.qmd#command-line-problems), or do the step in the browser. |

## Alternatives

- **Pair:** one person writes the data dictionary; the other corrects the citation file and writes the decision. Review each other's pull request.
- **Private path:** a release in a private repository is visible only to people with access. That is the right default until you decide to publish.
